text:
alex: RFC follow-up — hitting an edge where private deployment rejects hosted-style `fallback_model` in customer manifests. Who should translate vs reject? cc @kevin @maria

kevin: my take: adapter layer should do translation so control plane stays simple. adapter declares what it supports in a capability manifest.

maria: careful — Dedicated has reserved pools and placement rules. An adapter translating hosted->dedicated could accidentally break isolation or admission policies. translation needs policy checks.

alex: agreed. propose rule: adapters may translate only within the same hosting class by default (hosted->hosted, dedicated->dedicated, private->private). cross-class translations must be explicitly allowed by control plane policy. Example capability snippet:

```
capabilities: {
  "hosting_classes": ["hosted","dedicated"],
  "fallbacks": {
    "allowed": "same_class",  // options: strict, same_class, cross_class
    "mapped_variants": ["small","quantized"]
  }
}
```

kevin: also need telemetry for this: `translation_attempt`, `translation_accepted`, `translation_rejected` with reason codes.

tina: another axis: KMS/HSM constraints. Private might mandate customer KMS for model keys. adapters must surface KMS compatibility in the handshake.

kevin: propose adding `capability_manifest` fields: `kms_compat: ["kms-v1","hsm-a"]`, `fallback_policy: "same_class"`. adapters should host this at `/capabilities` and control plane fetches it during registration.

alex: sounds good. quick question: can we allow cross-class fallback for non-sensitive workloads (e.g., embeddings) as an exception? @tina

tina: embeddings are lower risk but not universally. we need a request-level `sensitivity` flag: `low|medium|high|pii`. cross-class allowed only for `low`.

maria: from implementation: adapters should return 4xx `unsupported_translation` for policy rejects. don't leak internal details; avoid 500s.

kevin: I'll prototype a JSON schema for the `capability_manifest` and add unit tests for the handshake parser. schema will include `hosting_classes`, `fallback_policy`, `kms_compat`, `observability_endpoints`.

alex: next steps: alex to draft a short RFC update capturing rule + example manifest, kevin to prototype schema + tests, tina to enumerate KMS/secret constraints per hosting class, maria to sanity-check error semantics. i'll consolidate into a decision doc and link back.

deploy-bot: Issue created: INF-4201 "Adapter translation policy flags" — https://redir/INF-4201

maria: :thumbsup: thanks all, this clears the immediate ambiguity.

kevin: one micro-impl note — prefer a lightweight capability probe (cached) rather than per-request fetch. keep latency impact minimal.

alex: yep. i'll include caching TTL in the RFC (suggest 5m). thanks everyone!
